items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: Pacific Flying Squid Populations Dropping in Korean Waters
items.summary: Study reports decline in Pacific flying squid populations in Korean waters, attributed to climate change. The post also references broader security topics.

items.title: FAA Ground Stop Issued Due to ‘Extraordinary Circumstances’
items.summary: FAA issues ground stop amid communications disruption; cause unclear, possible cyberattack under investigation.

items.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
items.summary: FBI warns of Artex tool enabling rapid cyberattacks; tool can chain techniques and reach privileged access in under three hours.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Researchers continue to find serious vulnerabilities in internet connected refrigerators
items.summary: Researchers identify 14 critical vulnerabilities in Dixell internet‑connected refrigerators that allow root access; honeypots show widespread probing.

items.title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
items.summary: New AI-driven penetration testing platforms can automate reconnaissance, vulnerability testing, and follow‑on actions, lowering skill threshold and speeding intrusions when misused.

items.title: Industry guidelines for offensive cyber tools unveiled through international Pall Mall Process
items.summary: U.S. signs onto Pall Mall Process guidelines for commercial offensive cyber tools, aiming to set industry standards for spyware and other intrusion capabilities.

items.title: This year’s bug count just passed 100K
items.summary: Global software bug count surpassed 100,000 this year, highlighting growing data security challenges.

items.title: ArcticRAT Cybercrime Gang Profiles Victim Finances With AI
items.summary: ArcticRAT malware now uses AI to profile victim finances, expanding from crypto theft to full device control and advanced data analysis.

items.title: City of Osaka warns of data breach impacting 1 million as Japan reels from dozens of cyber incidents
items.summary: Osaka city warns residents of potential data breach affecting 1 million people; urges caution against suspicious government emails amid multiple cyber incidents.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix
items.summary: Trezor confirms malicious hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets sold by CryptoBilis; device firmware updated to mitigate theft of recovery phrases.

items.title: NYC to bar surveillance pricing as momentum for bans grows nationwide
items.summary: NYC will fine companies $1,000 for each verified instance of surveillance pricing. The measure is part of a national trend toward banning such pricing practices.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
items.summary: German defense technology firm Quantum Systems reported a cyberattack on its drone operations in late October. The attack was attributed to hostile actors.

items.title: University of Texas at Arlington warns personal information stolen during cyberattack
items.summary: University of Texas at Arlington confirmed that personal data was stolen in a cyberattack. The investigation identified the stolen data but did not disclose the specific information obtained.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE
items.summary: PostgreSQL released patches for 52 security flaws, including a 22‑year‑old bug (CVE‑2026‑6460) that enabled authenticated remote code execution. Fixing the flaw requires rebuilding any C-language extensions on the server.

items.title: MDR Pricing: Comparing Asset-Based and Ingestion-Based Costs
items.summary: MDR pricing comparisons show that similar annual budgets can provide different evidence access, retention periods, and responsibilities. These differences impact incident investigation and attacker tracing.

items.title: German parliament passes law giving spy agencies hacking, sabotage powers
items.summary: The German Bundestag approved a bill granting intelligence agencies expanded hacking and sabotage powers, marking the most significant postwar spy law overhaul.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Check Point gateways hacked via PHP2Shell to deploy VMware ESXi wiper
items.summary: Check Point Security Gateway instances were targeted with PHP2Shell attacks that deployed data‑wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts.

items.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents pay without seeing your card number
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, allowing agents to pay using a stand‑in card number so users' real card details remain hidden from agents and merchants.

items.title: New Mior and Skyfall Attacks Let Rogue Cloud Hosts Steal Secrets From AMD SEV-SNP VMs
items.summary: Two attacks, Mior and Skyfall, enable a malicious hypervisor to read and modify data inside AMD SEV‑SNP protected VMs. Mior also requires control of the server BIOS.

items.title: In Other News: New CISA Director Nominee, Connected Car Hacking, Baker Tilly Data Breach
items.summary: The article covers several cybersecurity developments, including a new CISA director nominee, connected‑car hacking incidents, and a Baker Tilly data breach.

items.title: How one AI agent exposed five critical enterprise security gaps
items.summary: An AI agent used for invoice processing can be manipulated via a malicious email to change vendor bank details without triggering alerts. Token Security identifies five critical gaps and offers guidance to prevent them.

items.title: Fake GTA 6 download goes after Steam logins and crypto wallet data
items.summary: A fake GTA 6 executable distributed through a Google Colab notebook contains a WARDEN Stealer loader that harvests saved passwords, browser cookies, Steam and Roblox credentials, and cryptocurrency wallet data.

items.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
items.summary: The FBI attributes more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft to North Korean threat actors using a deepfake video call scheme called FaceStealer over the past 18 months.

items.title: Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases
items.summary: Trezor discovered an implant in three Safe 5 wallets sold by CryptoBilis that reads recovery phrases from the screen and transmits them via mobile network to an attacker‑controlled server.

items.title: Microsoft Struggles to Restore Email and Other Services in a Global Outage
items.summary: Microsoft is working to restore email and other services after a global outage, using a measured approach to identify and repair affected infrastructure.

items.title: Hackers' Overreliance on AI Can Result in Weaker Cyber-Attacks, Proofpoint Researcher Says
items.summary: Proofpoint researcher notes that threat actors’ reliance on AI has introduced many mistakes, with no evidence of increased sophistication.

items.title: Quantum Systems drones back in the air after malware scare
items.summary: Germany’s Bundeswehr has lifted the precautionary grounding of Quantum Systems drones after a malicious update reached military servers.

items.title: Attackers in Binance Breach Targeted Known Weakness, Missing Controls
items.summary: Attackers in the Binance breach exploited a known weakness and missing controls, with blockchain sweepers hindering security measures.

items.title: Record number of cyber incidents reported to UK privacy regulator
items.summary: The UK privacy regulator recorded a record number of cyber incidents this year, with data extortion and AI cited as key drivers.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Apify Confirms Customer Data Accessed in Cyberattack
items.summary: Apify confirmed that an intruder accessed customer accounts and personal information during a cyberattack.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Set to Ramp up Security Risks to Organizations
items.summary: While Microsoft resolves the M365 and Outlook outage, cybersecurity teams warn that the incident could heighten security risks as attackers may exploit the chaos.

items.title: Microsoft says November security updates cause printing issues
items.summary: Microsoft warned that its November 2026 security updates could cause printing failures for documents with complex formatting.

items.title: SilentAir Hackers Intercept Calls, SMS From Inside Mobile Networks
items.summary: Enea reported that SilentAir hijacked mobile network nodes to intercept calls and SMS, targeting primarily Taiwanese subscribers.

items.title: AI Doesn’t Have to Go Rogue to Break the World
items.summary: An essay from DEF CON 34 discusses AI hacking, including people hacking AI, using AI to hack other systems, and AI systems hacking independently.

items.title: When an AI Agent Goes Wrong, Can You Stop It?
items.summary: An AI agent tasked with sorting support tickets can export records to an unfamiliar destination because it has the necessary access and tools. The scenario highlights uncertainty around how to halt an autonomous agent. The incident underscores the need for clear control mechanisms.

items.title: Apple details Secure Exclaves, isolated runtimes for camera and microphone data
items.summary: Apple unveiled Secure Exclaves, a security architecture that isolates camera and microphone data during background processing. Data processed within the enclaves is inaccessible to the main OS, apps, or Apple itself. The feature powers person recognition on HomeView, Siri Recap, and Live Rewind.

items.title: Phishing Rises Three Times Faster in Europe Than Globally, Proofpoint Finds
items.summary: Proofpoint research indicates phishing incidents in Europe increased 4.5 times year over year, compared to a 1.5 times rise globally. The data suggests a growing threat landscape in the region.

items.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
items.summary: The SilentAir group hijacked telecom equipment in several Asian operators to intercept calls and SMS, targeting Taiwanese users. Enea traced the attack sources to at least six countries and identified the group as a likely state-sponsored actor.

items.title: 354 dark web vendors and buyers arrested in Operation TorNado
items.summary: Operation TorNado saw 354 dark‑web vendors and buyers arrested across 14 countries, following investigations of five defunct marketplaces. Europol and national police seized assets and disrupted ongoing trade.

items.title: Crackdown on UK medical record snooping after staff reported sneaking 300+ times this year
items.summary: A watchdog has requested assurances from 200 UK healthcare executives that employees are not inappropriately accessing patient records. The inquiry follows reports of staff snooping on files over 300 times this year.

items.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
items.summary: Operation Endgame dismantled servers used by Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware, and seized 6.4 million stolen credentials belonging to more than 40,000 victims.

items.title: NATO issues and then withdraws Russian taxi app travel advice for defense industry conference
items.summary: NATO initially advised conference attendees to use the Russian‑owned Yandex Go app for travel, but later retracted the recommendation amid concerns over Kremlin data access.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Law Enforcement Disrupts Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC Infrastructure
items.summary: Law enforcement seized 235 servers and 257 domains linked to Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC, and recovered 6.4 million victim credentials during Operation Endgame.

items.title: Check Point warns of zero-day flaw exploited for root access
items.summary: Check Point issued emergency hotfixes for a high‑severity zero‑day flaw that has been exploited to gain root access and establish persistence on vulnerable devices since late October.

items.title: Brit police watchdog says cops' use of facial recog risks wrongful arrests
items.summary: UK police watchdog warns that facial‑recognition use by police can lead to wrongful arrests due to governance gaps and officers’ misunderstanding of the technology’s limits.

items.title: Citrix Patches 10 Critical NetScaler Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Citrix released patches for ten critical NetScaler vulnerabilities that could allow exploitation resulting in unexpected behavior or denial‑of‑service conditions.

items.title: Microsoft confirms Windows activation failures after November updates
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that its November Patch Tuesday updates are causing Windows activation and licensing failures, producing error code 0x80041008.

items.title: OpenAI’s Daybreak brings AI agents to security testing and vulnerability fixes
items.summary: OpenAI launched Daybreak, AI agents that perform web‑application penetration testing and help investigate vulnerabilities and develop fixes through its Red Team and Defense Factory modules.

items.title: OpenAI Unveils Daybreak Red Team, Defense Factory Security Tools
items.summary: Daybreak Red Team uses AI agents to pentest web applications, while Defense Factory analyzes findings and prepares patches for remediation.

items.title: AI Set to Revolutionize Ransomware Following “Stagnant” Few Years
items.summary: TrendAI analyst Bob McArdle predicts ransomware techniques will evolve significantly in the next year, with AI making attacks more dangerous and profitable.

items.title: Ransomware at the hypervisor layer: how attackers use ESXi and vCenter features for malicious purposes
items.summary: Kaspersky experts explain how ransomware targets VMware ESXi and vCenter, noting the hypervisor layer is hard to monitor and outlining common access paths and protection strategies.

items.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops Windows Zero-Day Exploit ‘SignDrop’
items.summary: Nightmare Eclipse released the SignDrop zero‑day exploit that abuses CLFS and Windows Defender to create arbitrary files in the context of the antimalware process.

items.title: Police arrest 354 suspects in dark web cybercrime crackdown
items.summary: International law enforcement arrested 354 suspects linked to vendors and buyers on several dark‑web marketplaces, including Archetyp, Nemesis, Tor2Door, Bohemia, and Kingdom.

items.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files
items.summary: Threat actors used PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in Check Point Gateways and a local privilege escalation flaw in Gaia OS to install the TSGA backdoor and delete ESXi files, targeting Israeli organizations since October 30, 2026.

items.title: Policy and Disclosure: 2026 Edition
items.summary: Project Zero's 90+30 disclosure policy gives vendors 90 days to patch vulnerabilities plus 30 days for rollout, but AI‑assisted discovery has altered the threat landscape.

items.title: PHP2Shell Exploited in Destructive Check Point Gateway Attacks
items.summary: PHP2Shell was used for initial compromise of Check Point gateways. CVE-2026-123039 allowed attackers to elevate privileges to root, leading to destructive attacks.

items.title: C++26 stumbles at finish line over Contracts dispute
items.summary: ISO working group is debating C++26 contracts. The dispute centers on runtime checks, complexity, and the release timetable.

items.title: Hackers Exploit New N-central Zero-Day Hours After PoC Publication
items.summary: 4EverAble2Shell flaw allows remote, unauthenticated code execution with root privileges. Exploited within hours of PoC release.

items.title: Stolen webcam clips of 900+ victims feed North Korea’s $400 million fake Zoom scheme
items.summary: North Korean hackers use stolen webcam footage to lure victims into fake Zoom/Teams calls, stealing over $400M in crypto. FBI calls scheme FaceStealer and has seized 900+ recordings.

items.title: How attackers turned a Teams meeting booking into a device code phishing trap
items.summary: Attackers used fake Teams meeting scheduler to trick employee into approving device code sign‑in, obtaining session token. Huntress identified incident after token acquisition.

items.title: Suspected North Korean IT workers reached onboarding at companies with open data
items.summary: Material Security traced 27 fabricated North Korean IT personas to onboarding in monitored organizations. One company exposed 277,000 SSNs via shared files.

items.title: Hackers Exploit N-central Flaws to Infect 21 Servers, Including 19 Running Hotfix 2
items.summary: N-able disclosed new 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell flaws. 21 servers infected, 19 running Hotfix 2; company restricted features while remediating.

items.title: Your pinned MCP server may not be as pinned as you think
items.summary: MCP server ran 15 different dependency sets over five weeks despite fixed release configuration. 23 of 69 packages changed, including cryptography and JWT libraries.

items.title: Digital sovereignty leaves enterprises chasing their own audit trails
items.summary: IBM survey shows 94% of enterprises faced digital sovereignty challenges in past three years. 91% had to prove control during events, 81% provided formal evidence to regulators.

items.title: FBI Says US Seized $1.2 Billion Worth of Cryptocurrency Stolen From Binance
items.summary: FBI seized $1.2B in crypto stolen from Binance. North Korean hackers also blamed for $400M theft via social engineering.

items.title: US seizes North Korean hacking infrastructure, $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance
items.summary: The US seized infrastructure linked to APT38, which used video call deception to steal $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance.

items.title: Fake Zillow pages use ClickFix NetSupport RAT to target apartment hunters
items.summary: Fake Zillow apartment review pages were used to deliver ClickFix NetSupport RAT to visitors, prompting them to copy and run a PowerShell command that installed remote‑control software on Windows machines.

items.title: PostgreSQL security update fixes 52 vulnerabilities, ends support for PostgreSQL 14
items.summary: PostgreSQL released versions 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25, addressing 52 security bugs and ending support for PostgreSQL 14; the fixes target memory errors and type‑confusion vulnerabilities in PL/Perl, PL/Tcl, and text‑search functions.

items.title: New worm-like 'SCKit' malware targets MSPs in ScreenConnect attacks
items.summary: SCKit, a worm‑like toolkit, was deployed in recent ScreenConnect attacks against managed service providers, spreading from infected customer devices to MSP technicians’ computers and compromising additional managed networks.

items.title: Getting Past the Post-Quantum Cryptography Discovery Phase
items.summary: Many organizations lack visibility into their cryptographic assets, making it difficult to determine where to begin transitioning to post‑quantum cryptography.

items.title: Hackers compromise 4,800 GitHub accounts to steal cloud credentials
items.summary: The 'wfx-loot' campaign used 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to scan 61,764 repositories, open pull requests, and push malware that steals cloud credentials.

items.title: Feds announce seizure of $1.2 billion from Binance theft; also takedown of ‘FaceStealer’ tools
items.summary: The DOJ and FBI seized $1.2 billion linked to a North Korea‑related cryptocurrency theft operation and dismantled the FaceStealer credential‑stealing tools.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Cyber Experts Weigh In: How to Fight Artex & AntiFox
items.summary: Cybersecurity experts recommend immediate defense planning to counter Artex and AntiFox, which use agentic pen‑testing tools to compromise systems.

items.title: Rogue remote-access campaign spread through ScreenConnect add-on, researchers say
items.summary: Researchers traced a worm‑like toolkit to a ScreenConnect add‑on, prompting ConnectWise to disable five third‑party extensions across 400 partner environments.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Exchange Online and Teams
items.summary: A Microsoft 365 outage caused by failed server health checks disrupted Outlook, Exchange Online, and Teams; Microsoft is investigating the cause and has found no evidence of a cyberattack.

items.title: OpenAI launches security products, tells orgs they’re doomed if they don’t use them
items.summary: OpenAI introduced new security products and warned organizations that failure to adopt them could leave them vulnerable to AI‑driven cyberattacks.

items.title: Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot worldwide
items.summary: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage affected Outlook, Teams, and Copilot globally, with Microsoft investigating the issue and users reporting connectivity problems.

items.title: Extortion Group Luna Moth Flits Into Law Firms a Second Time
items.summary: Extortion group Luna Moth targets law firms that did not pay the first ransom. The attack uses social engineering to steal Microsoft access tokens.

items.title: Lego marketplace BrickLink in pieces after 'unusual activity' takes it offline for almost a week
items.summary: Lego marketplace BrickLink has been offline for almost a week after unusual activity. No confirmed cause has been announced.

items.title: New N-able "4EverAble2Shell" zero-day exploited hours after PoC released
items.summary: N‑able zero‑day "4EverAble2Shell" was exploited within hours of the PoC release. At least 21 systems were affected, including 19 with the latest security update, and attackers deployed cryptocurrency miners.

items.title: United to block customers from using AI agents, citing cyber threats
items.summary: United Airlines has blocked customers from using AI agents. The airline cites risks of credential sharing and unintended purchases.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Never be afraid to ask questions
items.summary: Amy reflects on an anthropology course that taught the importance of asking questions to bridge cultural gaps.

items.title: Shipping giant Maersk says recent cyber incident affected legacy system
items.summary: Maersk reports a cyber incident that affected its legacy system. The incident is part of a series of attacks on shipping ports, following ransomware on Brazil’s largest port.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents keeps agent credentials in your environment
items.summary: Anthropic released a self‑hosted version of Claude Managed Agents. Companies can run the agent harness, sandboxes, credentials, and session history in their own environment; the private beta began on November 12.

items.title: Software Samaritan revamps borked Indian certs to block smart TV ads
items.summary: Software Samaritan altered Indian certificates to block Samsung TV ads and tracking. A firmware fix later removed the effect.

items.title: ThreatsDay: 59 Linux Kernel Bugs, Falcon Spyware, GSocket Backdoors + 17 More Stories
items.summary: ThreatsDay highlighted 59 Linux kernel bugs, Falcon spyware, GSocket backdoors, and other stories. The report notes attackers using fake sites, stolen access, and trusted tools, with AI accelerating attacks.

items.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
items.summary: The new SignDrop zero‑day exploits the Windows CLFS driver to give local users SYSTEM privileges. It abuses path redirection to control privileged processes.

items.title: Don’t put Section 702 spying law renewal in defense bill, groups urge Hill leaders
items.summary: Civil liberties groups urged lawmakers to exclude Section 702 renewal from the defense bill. They argue the law expands U.S. surveillance powers. The letter was sent to congressional leaders.

items.title: International operation dismantles malware networks, exposes 6.4 million stolen credentials
items.summary: Operation Endgame dismantled ransomware supply‑chain malware, including loaders and remote‑access trojans. The action exposed 6.4 million stolen credentials. The operation was a joint international effort.

items.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Lets Attackers Read and Overwrite All Private Container Images in a Registry
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay allows attackers to read and overwrite private container images. The flaw works even with anonymous access enabled or with a valid account. Red Hat released fixed builds for eight Quay versions.

items.title: European authorities take down SteaIC malware servers for second time this year
items.summary: German authorities seized SteaIC malware servers linked to the Virtualine hosting provider. The takedown was the second time the servers were targeted this year. The operation involved cooperation with Dutch police and the FBI.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ConnectWise investigates ScreenConnect breaches after reports of incidents at nearly 50 organizations
items.summary: ConnectWise confirmed breaches of its ScreenConnect tool affecting almost 50 organizations. The incidents were caused by abuse of a third‑party tool. The company is investigating the incidents.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: New Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
items.summary: A new Windows zero‑day exploit, SignDrop, can grant attackers SYSTEM privileges. The vulnerability was discovered by researcher Abdelhamid Naceri. It allows privilege escalation on affected systems.

items.title: Weak Passwords Expose SQL Servers to Cryptominer and Gh0st RAT
items.summary: Fortinet identified weak passwords on SQL Server instances that enabled delivery of a cryptominer and the Gh0st RAT. The vulnerability allows attackers to install malicious software via compromised credentials.

items.title: Citrix Patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client Flaws, Including Authentication Bypass
items.summary: Citrix released patches for 12 critical flaws in NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway, and Secure Access Client. Vulnerabilities could lead to denial‑of‑service or authentication bypass. CVE‑2026‑120868 has a CVSS score of 9.3.

items.title: Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google
items.summary: Apache fixed a critical remote‑code‑execution flaw, CVE‑2026‑119618, in the mod_http2 module. The race condition allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. The patch was released after discovery by Anthropic and Google.

items.title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
items.summary: Researchers found 186 fake AI‑tool domains that redirect users to ClickFix lures, browser‑hijacking malware, and search‑hijacking extensions. The campaign, called TypoPrompting, exploits users’ trust in familiar AI names.

items.title: WhiteArmor gang claims responsibility for latest cyber attack on shipping giant Maersk
items.summary: WhiteArmor gang claims responsibility for a cyber attack that compromised a Maersk system and stole data.

items.title: Police dismantle Gootloader, CastleRAT, StealC malware infrastructure
items.summary: Europol and partners seized hundreds of servers and domains used by Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware operations.

items.title: Picus puts AI agents on the offensive with autonomous pentesting
items.summary: Picus Security launched autonomous penetration testing agents that simulate attacker behavior to identify vulnerabilities under governance controls.

items.title: Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors
items.summary: Unit 42 reported attackers used the open-source Cairn AI framework to autonomously breach semiconductor, defense, and civic targets.

items.title: Attackers breached 10 organizations with an open-source AI pentest framework
items.summary: Chinese-speaking attackers used the Cairn AI framework to conduct 25 operations, breaching 10 organizations with minimal input.

items.title: Your Endpoint Management Platform Could Be Your Biggest Security Risk
items.summary: Compromised endpoint management platforms can become powerful attack tools; customer-controlled cryptographic authorization can mitigate this risk.

items.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
items.summary: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are permanently vulnerable, urging immediate upgrade or migration.

items.title: Hijacked email accounts complicate investigations into European bomb hoaxes
items.summary: Bomb threats sent to thousands of schools across Europe originated from a compromised email account at a Taiwanese university, following a pattern of hoax threats targeting airports and newsrooms via legitimate institutions.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Apify rotates API tokens, prompts 2FA resets after breach
items.summary: Apify detected unauthorized access to internal systems, rotated critical secrets, revoked some third‑party OAuth connections, and required users to reset 2FA.

items.title: Hacked Asian Telcos Used to Intercept Taiwanese Calls and Texts
items.summary: Enea linked SilentAir and Liminal Panda to attacks on Asian mobile operators that were used to intercept calls and texts in Taiwan.

items.title: Lego Takes BrickLink Marketplace Offline After Detecting Unusual Activity
items.summary: Lego shut down its BrickLink Marketplace following detection of unusual activity while investigating the incident.

items.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch Over 180 Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Google released Chrome 157 fixing 83 vulnerabilities, and Mozilla released Firefox 160 addressing 99 bugs, together patching over 180 security issues.

items.title: Attacker Targets 60,000 GitHub Repositories in Credential Theft Campaign
items.summary: The wfx-loot campaign deployed a CI secret stealer across more than 1,800 GitHub repositories, affecting up to 60,000 repositories through hijacked accounts.

items.title: Operation Endgame malware takedown turns up over 6 million stolen logins
items.summary: Police and Europol dismantled servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware, recovering over 6 million stolen credentials from infected computers.

items.title: Romania says it stopped Russian cyberattack targeting government emails
items.summary: Romania’s intelligence agency halted a Russian state‑linked cyber‑espionage campaign before the attackers could exfiltrate sensitive government email data.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Daylight Lands $80 Million for AI-Powered Security Operations
items.summary: Daylight secured $80 million in funding to accelerate product development, hire talent, expand its U.S. presence, and enter new markets.

items.title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths
items.summary: SCKit malware exploits CVE-2026-84869 in ScreenConnect to turn remote support sessions into attack vectors.

items.title: Hackers exploiting ScreenConnect plugin flaw to spread malware across hundreds of PCs
items.summary: ConnectWise disabled third‑party extensions in 400 environments after bughunters discovered an authentication flaw that could let attackers bypass MFA and spread malware via the ScreenConnect plugin.

items.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments
items.summary: Suspected Kazakhstan-linked hackers used an AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments, steal sensitive documents, and infiltrate critical infrastructure networks.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that Windows updates released since October 2026 Patch Tuesday are causing SQL Server performance and stability issues.

items.title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs
items.summary: Google Cloud warned that three side‑channel flaws in AMD Turin CPUs could allow a VM to read data from other processes or the kernel, and recommends guest OS patches and reboot.

items.title: Another Way Police Are Locating People from Their Smartphones
items.summary: Penlink’s Webloc tool collects location data from weather, gaming, email, and religious apps on smartphones and sells the service to police, enabling detailed tracking over the past year.

items.title: Webinar: See How Identity Blind Spots Put Your SOC at Risk and How to Close Them
items.summary: The webinar discusses how identity blind spots can expose SOCs to risk, emphasizing the need to quickly identify actors behind suspicious activity and the potential for AI agents to misuse permissions.

items.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
items.summary: N‑able reported new vulnerabilities in N‑central 2026.4.1 HF2 that allow remote code execution and SYSTEM access when the Legacy API is exposed to the internet.

items.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
items.summary: Material Security identified a phishing campaign that hijacked live Google sessions via calendar invites and live proxies, and has taken down hundreds of attacker domains.

items.title: PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution
items.summary: PTC released patches for CVE‑2026‑126325, a critical flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM that could allow remote code execution through improper input validation and deserialization.

items.title: European tech buyers add digital sovereignty to cyber shopping list
items.summary: EU tech buyers are prioritizing digital sovereignty in procurement decisions, influenced by NIS2, DORA, and other regulatory factors.

items.title: Notion Customer Data Compromised in Fireworks AI Hack
items.summary: The Fireworks AI hack compromised chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces, with most transcripts unattributable.

items.title: Microsoft Entra adds a seven-day safeguard against irreversible identity deletion
items.summary: Microsoft Entra preview feature Hard Deletion Protection gives administrators a seven‑day window to recover selected identities before permanent deletion. It applies to cloud‑only users, groups, and applications.

items.title: Stolen Claude API keys can turn Claude Code into a remote-controlled implant
items.summary: Darktrace researchers showed that stolen Claude API keys can redirect Claude Code into a remote‑controlled implant, enabling exfiltration of large files via the Claude Files API.

items.title: Inside an AI Attack Against a US Retailer
items.summary: Attackers used AI‑generated scripts to achieve lateral movement within a US retailer’s network after hand‑typed commands failed, breaching the system in minutes.

items.title: Security Teams Must Shift from Patching to Mitigation in the AI Era
items.summary: Symantec’s Dick O’Brien argues that the shrinking patch window forces organizations to adopt an assume‑exploit mindset and focus on mitigation rather than patching.

items.title: Hackers Deploy Malware in Fresh ScreenConnect Campaign
items.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a legitimate ScreenConnect extension to bypass authentication and deploy malware, as reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that November 2026 security updates fail to install on Windows 11 systems running the October preview update, affecting update reliability.

items.title: Photos: IRISSCON 2026 cybercrime conference
items.summary: IRISSCON 2026, held at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium, showcased current cyber threats and practical response strategies, with industry partners such as Help Net Security in attendance.

items.title: Transcending the trust boundaries: how a cloud pentest works
items.summary: The article introduces a series on cloud penetration testing, covering external, overlay, and underlay layers, common architectures like OpenStack and Kubernetes, typical attack chains, and real‑world incidents.

items.title: NCSC Launches Cyber Adversary Testing to Boost Resilience
items.summary: The UK National Cyber Security Centre launched a Cyber Adversary Simulation scheme to test and improve organizations’ cyber resilience.

items.title: Hackers Target N-central Zero-Days as N-able Rushes Patches
items.summary: After a researcher disclosed over 30 zero‑days, hackers targeted N‑central while N‑able released patches for unauthenticated vulnerabilities, as reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
items.summary: Threat actors use GSocket, a legitimate open‑source remote access tool, to maintain persistence on Linux servers even after initial vulnerabilities are patched. The tool is embedded to keep access.

items.title: AWS Emulator: Open-source tool for testing AWS apps locally, built by autonomous AI agents
items.summary: AWS released AWS Emulator, a free open‑source tool that simulates AWS services locally. It was written entirely by autonomous AI agents, with no engineer code, and incurs no extra service fee.

items.title: London hotel put admin login for booking website on whiteboard behind the front desk
items.summary: A London hotel displayed the admin login credentials for its booking website on a whiteboard behind the front desk, exposing them to anyone in the lobby.

items.title: Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover
items.summary: MongoDB Server has a pre‑authentication flaw (CVE‑2026‑118383) that lets attackers send two requests to crash the server. The crash occurs when the server later becomes primary during failover. Fixed versions were released.

items.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Could Expose Private Container Images
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay allows attackers to steal private container images, overwrite repositories, and maintain persistent access. Red Hat has issued a patch.

items.title: Maersk Reveals Data Breach as Extortion Group Demands $5m
items.summary: Maersk announced that a threat actor extracted data from a legacy system and an extortion group demanded $5 million for the data.

items.title: Maersk Confirms Data Theft Amid $5 Million Extortion Attempt
items.summary: Maersk confirmed that the WhiteArmor ransomware group stole 100 GB of data from its systems and that the group is demanding $5 million in ransom.

items.title: .NET 11 security changes target the software supply chain
items.summary: Microsoft released .NET 11, a Standard Term Support release that focuses on software supply‑chain integrity, authentication handling, and platform lifecycle. It includes updates to C# 15, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows development.

items.title: Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data
items.summary: Node.js fixed 16 vulnerabilities, including two HTTP/2 bugs that could crash servers or leak memory contents to other connections. Updated versions are available for 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Autofix and the question of who owns a bad AI patch
items.summary: GitHub’s VP discussed accountability for AI‑generated patches that fix one flaw but introduce another, explaining how Agentic Autofix re‑runs detection engines and tests, and advising CISOs on metrics and codebase readiness.

items.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
items.summary: An attacker used 4,837 stolen GitHub accounts to deploy a CI secret stealer in over 1,800 repositories, harvesting credentials.

items.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
items.summary: A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module (CVE-2026-119618) allows unauthenticated remote code execution on affected versions.

items.title: ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients
items.summary: ConnectWise disabled five third‑party extensions after reports of unauthorized access via rogue ScreenConnect clients; no evidence of infrastructure compromise was found.

items.title: Disgraced former CA eMudhra blames buggy script for hopelessly weak certificates
items.summary: eMudhra's former chief attributes weak certificates to a faulty script, citing hardware shortages that forced a workaround.

items.title: Chinese AI Project Scouts Spies in Taiwan Chip Industry
items.summary: The Chinese Communist Party built a big‑data system to gather information on Taiwanese chip industry personnel, potentially to target and exploit them.

items.title: Smashing Security podcast #492: How hackers turned Russian cars into pumpkins
items.summary:
Podcast discusses car hacking via digital keys, a $550 ransom. 
Also covers deepfake scheme that stole $130M. 
Highlights human factor vulnerabilities.

items.title: Japan Pushes Emergency Funding for Cybersecurity as AI-Assisted Breaches Rise
items.summary: Japan pushes emergency funding for cybersecurity, adding public‑private responders, an AI‑focused team, and expanded use of active cyber‑defense powers.

items.title: Baker Tilly notifies clients of data breach at third-party provider
items.summary: Baker Tilly Advisory Group informs clients of a data breach that compromised personal information of clients and their dependents.

items.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
items.summary: Unit 42 reports on attacker use of AI‑powered red team tools (ARTEX) and offers mitigation guidance for defenders.

items.title: Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, impact dozens of organizations
items.summary: ConnectWise investigates a malware campaign targeting MSPs via compromised ScreenConnect environments to deploy rogue remote‑access clients.

items.title: Attackers Say 'Hello' to a Different Scale of Cloud Attack
items.summary: Researchers identify a cloud attack chain dubbed "Greeter" where attackers leave "hello" messages in logs to obscure their trail.

items.title: eMudhra revokes 8 more CA certificates after private key mishap
items.summary: eMudhra revokes eight additional intermediate CA certificates after discovering improper private key handling during certificate generation.

items.title: AI Raises the Stakes for Cyber Resilience
items.summary: AI‑driven threats increase the importance of rapid business disruption recovery as a competitive advantage.

items.title: Notion says Fireworks breach exposed customer AI chat transcripts
items.summary: Notion disclosed that a breach at AI provider Fireworks AI exposed Notion AI chat transcripts in a limited number of workspaces.

items.title: N-able Takes N-central Platform Offline After Discovery of 33 Flaws
items.summary: N‑able takes its N‑central platform offline after finding 33 flaws, releasing a hotfix to mitigate public exploits.

items.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
items.summary: Investigation points to a 36‑year‑old man in St. Petersburg as the administrator of ransomware group Qilin, which has claimed at least 365 victims in three months.

items.title: N-able Rushes Out N-central Fixes After 33 Zero-Days Go Public
items.summary: N‑able released seven fixes for N‑central after 33 zero‑day vulnerabilities were publicly disclosed, addressing the identified CVEs to secure the platform.

items.title: Iran-backed network directed London attacks over FaceTime, US prosecutors say
items.summary: U.S. prosecutors allege an Iran‑backed group directed attacks via FaceTime against Jewish and U.S. sites, including synagogues in Belgium, the Netherlands and London, and U.S. bank buildings in Amsterdam and Paris.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Anthropic's Glasswing Finds Many Vulnerabilities Yet Delivers Few Fixes, Researcher Says
items.summary: Patrick Garrity reports that Anthropic’s Glasswing program has resulted in only 217 of the thousands of vulnerabilities reported being fixed after seven months.

items.title: Today: CISO Forum Virtual Summit 2026 Day 2 – Join Cybersecurity Leaders Online
items.summary: The CISO Forum Virtual Summit 2026 Day 2 invites cybersecurity leaders to discuss risk management and defense strategies in a two‑day online event.

items.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
items.summary: Maersk confirmed a data breach after a threat actor accessed a legacy system inherited from an acquisition and extracted data, with WhiteArmor ransomware demanding a $5 million payment.

items.title: Critical Zoom Workplace Flaw Could Allow Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Zoom released updates for Zoom Workplace for Windows to fix two critical flaws, including CVE‑2026‑108186, which could allow unauthenticated privilege escalation.

items.title: Suspected Chinese Malware Supplier Tied to Three Hacking Campaigns
items.summary: Check Point identified a China‑based malware supplier linked to three hacking campaigns that share the Sparrow malware framework.

items.title: Critical Xen Orchestra Flaws Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: Critical authentication bypasses in Xen Orchestra allow attackers to execute arbitrary code as admin and take over XCP‑ng nodes, and these vulnerabilities have been actively exploited.

items.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
items.summary: Researchers found that the AntiFox AI penetration testing platform was used to steal AWS credentials and pivot laterally, with attacks originating from Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces.

items.title: Hackers use AntiFox AI agents in AWS credential-theft attacks
items.summary: Attackers are hosting self‑managed AntiFox instances on Alibaba Cloud to target web services and AWS environments, facilitating credential theft.

items.title: eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice
items.summary: Linux eBPF rootkits enable malicious activity to hide without loading kernel modules. Flare reports that underground forums share rootkit source code, tutorials, and exploits targeting Linux systems.

items.title: The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar
items.summary: Falcon C2 is a browser-based threat framework that targets governments through malicious scripts, extensions, and the Antino implant.

items.title: Kai extends Autonomous Defense Platform visibility to internet-facing assets
items.summary: Kai announced External Attack Surface Management (EASM) on its Autonomous Defense Platform and launched Kai Labs to research AI‑driven security challenges, unifying internal and external exposure visibility.

items.title: Git fixes six vulnerabilities, including code execution during recursive clones
items.summary: Git released security updates for six vulnerabilities that could allow code execution, unintended file writes, or memory corruption when processing malicious repositories.

items.title: Blind trust: stealing credentials through CSP
items.summary: Content Security Policy can fail to prevent XSS when a policy allows‑lists a domain, enabling attackers to steal credentials via HTML injection.

items.title: Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits
items.summary: Threat actors targeted Qlik Sense servers, attempting PowerShell reverse shells and exploiting ActiveMQ and Veeam vulnerabilities across EU customers.

items.title: Asus, Zoom Release Security Patches
items.summary: Asus and Zoom issued security patches for vulnerabilities that could lead to command execution, memory overwrites, and privilege escalation.

items.title: Embed Security lets analysts teach its AI SOC Platform how to investigate
items.summary: Embed Security added features that let teams train its AI SOC platform with custom investigation steps, expanded memory, and detection engineering.
